text:
Maya CS: Quick update — ArborHealth preflight for their private/VPC rollout. They finished the network peer but security wants an explicit KMS key policy review and confirmation we can forward audit logs to their SIEM (Splunk hosted) over an approved egress. Also: they asked for minimal firewall port list for the inference nodes (ingress from LB, outbound to telemetry). Can we get a quick checklist and any blockers? @Owen NetEng @Priya Security @Sam Solutions

Owen NetEng: Thanks — I looked at their VPC peering config. Basic notes:
- Ingress to model fleet should only allow from their internal LB subnet (10.8.32.0/24).
- Control plane egress: 443 to our control-plane-proxy IPs (we'll provide).
- Telemetry/metrics -> 443 to telemetry.redwood.example.com (we route via NAT).
- Ports list for customers: 443 (control + telemetry), 22 (jump host only, locked), 5000-5002 TCP for internal model health checks (optional).
I can provide a short HCL snippet for their infra team.

Priya Security: Re: KMS — their initial policy attempts to grant broad principals. We need the key policy to:
1) Restrict CreateGrant/RetireGrant to our service principal, not the customer.
2) Allow AWS logs delivery role to use Encrypt/Decrypt only for envelopes.
3) Add an explicit Deny for DeleteKey unless from a root/admin OIDC role.
Here's a minimal example they can adapt:

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodServiceUse",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::REDFO:role/redwood-inference-service"},
      "Action": ["kms:Encrypt","kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    },
    {
      "Sid": "RestrictGrants",
      "Effect": "Deny",
      "Principal": "*",
      "Action": ["kms:CreateGrant","kms:RetireGrant"],
      "Condition": {"StringNotEquals": {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::REDFO:role/redwood-inference-service"}}
    }
  ]
}
```

Priya Security: Also need their audit logs destination info (Splunk HEC endpoint + token TTL) and confirmation they will use TLS with cert validation.

Sam Solutions: I'll author the short runbook for handoff. High level steps:
1) Provide LB subnet CIDR and LB FQDN to Owen.
2) Customer adds firewall rule: allow inbound 443 from LB CIDR to fleet ENIs.
3) Customer provides Splunk HEC URL + token. We test ingest via staging forwarder.
4) Customer shares IAM role ARN for log delivery and we confirm the KMS policy binds to that role.
5) Run a one-hour smoke: generate sample requests, verify KV cache warm, verify audit entries show in Splunk.
I can draft terraform notes like:```hcl
resource "aws_security_group_rule" "allow_inbound_from_lb" {
  type = "ingress"
  cidr_blocks = ["10.8.32.0/24"]
  from_port = 443
  to_port = 443
  protocol = "tcp"
}
```
I will also include rollback steps (revoke peering, remove LB route).

infra-bot: CI check: "arborhealth-preflight" pipeline passed 7/8 tests; failing test: splunk-hec-connectivity. Logs: 
- tls_handshake_error -> remote cert CN mismatch.
- token expired -> 401 on initial request.
Link to pipeline: https://ci.redwood/integrations/arborhealth/123

Maya CS: Ok — action items:
- @Owen please publish the minimal ports + NAT IPs to the ticket and attach the HCL snippet.
- @Priya update the KMS policy example to include STS conditions for the customer's log-delivery role.
- @Sam schedule the one-hour smoke window once Splunk cert/token issues are resolved.
I pinged the customer about cert rotation and asked them to reissue a HEC token with a 90d TTL.

Owen NetEng: Will do today, pinging infra to allocate NAT IPs. ETA 4pm PT. :thumbsup:

Priya Security: I'll add the STS condition and push to the ticket. Also recommend they add a short note in their audit SOP showing how to validate our service principal usage.

Sam Solutions: I'll tentatively book Wed 10–11am PT for the smoke and mark as tentative until Splunk is green.

Maya CS: Thanks team — if infra-bot shows splunk-hec-connectivity green after cert/token, I'll send a go/no-go to the customer. :rocket:
